sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark (fill in the blanks, true/false, one word or phrase, match).

questions.q: Answer in a phrase: (a) Who wrote Orders of Infinity? (b) Which Indian was the first to be elected Fellow of Trinity College?
Answer in a phrase: (a) What is the Raman Effect? (b) Name any two Raman lines property.
questions.answer: (a) When monochromatic light passes through a transparent substance it scatters with two weak spectral lines, showing light is made of photons. (b) Two lines of very low intensity parallel to the incident line.

Answer in a phrase: (a) What does the Crescograph record? (b) What did it prove about plants?
questions.answer: (a) Plant growth and movement to a millionth of a millimetre. (b) That plants have a circulatory system.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in about 25 words.

questions.q: Why did C.V. Raman win the Nobel Prize?
questions.answer: For discovering the Raman Effect – the scattering of light with spectral lines proving that light is made of photons – in 1930.

questions.q: Name the instrument invented by J.C. Bose and its use.
questions.answer: The Crescograph; it records even a millionth part of a millimetre of plant growth and movement and showed plants have a circulatory system.

questions.q: Why is Homi Bhabha called the father of Indian nuclear science?
questions.answer: He founded TIFR (1945), BARC at Trombay and the reactor Apsara and was the first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission.

questions.q: Name five defence projects developed by Dr Abdul Kalam.
questions.answer: Prithvi, Trishul, Akash, Nag and Agni.

questions.q: How did Kalam's research help the polio-affected?
questions.answer: Light carbon material designed for Agni reduced the weight of calipers from 4 kg to 400 g.

questions.q: What was Vikram Sarabhai's contribution to space research?
questions.answer: He chaired INCOSPAR, set up TERLS at Thumba and was the main person behind India's first satellite Aryabhata.

questions.q: Why was Ramanujan sent to London?
questions.answer: G.H. Hardy recognised his genius from the 120 theorems in his letter and arranged his passage to Trinity College, Cambridge.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 40–50 words.

questions.q: Describe any three contributions of Srinivasa Ramanujan.
questions.answer: He published a research paper on Bernoulli numbers (1911) and solved problems in the Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society; with G.H. Hardy and J.E. Littlewood he made amazing contributions in Cambridge and published many papers; he left the three notebooks of results and became FRS and the first Indian Fellow of Trinity College.

questions.q: Describe the achievements of J.C. Bose.
questions.answer: He studied electric waves and was knighted (1917) and became FRS (1920); he invented the Crescograph recording plant growth; his instruments showed that metals respond to stimuli and tire; and he invented the first wireless coherer before Marconi.

questions.q: Explain the Raman Effect.
questions.answer: When a single-coloured (monochromatic) beam passes through a transparent substance, it scatters; Raman found two weak spectral lines parallel to the incident light, so the scattered light was not monochromatic. The phenomenon is the Raman Effect and the lines are Raman lines; it proved that light is made of photons. He won the Nobel Prize in 1930.

questions.q: Write about the contribution of Dr Homi Bhabha.
questions.answer: Bhabha led India into the atomic age: he got TIFR founded at his ancestral home in 1945, started BARC at Trombay and the reactor Apsara, chaired the Atomic Energy Commission (1948) and the UN conference on peaceful uses of atomic energy, and won the Padma Bhushan.

questions.q: Describe the contributions of Vikram Sarabhai.
questions.answer: He studied cosmic rays under Raman, led the Aryabhata satellite project, founded industries and IIMs, chaired INCOSPAR and the Atomic Energy Commission, set up TERLS and planned satellite education for villages; he saved crores by producing antibiotics and military hardware in India.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 150–200 words.

questions.q: Examine the early life, education and first employment of Sir J.C. Bose.
questions.answer: Jagdish Chandra Bose was born on 30 November 1858 at Mymensingh (now in Bangladesh), where he had his early education, and studied at St Xavier's College, Calcutta. In 1885 he became Assistant Professor of Physics at Presidency College, but refused his salary because it was nearly half of an Englishman's. He decided to become a scientist to recover the fame India enjoyed in ancient times. He built apparatus to study electric waves.

or.q: Examine the inventions and achievements of Sir J.C. Bose as a scientist.
or.answer: He invented the Crescograph, which records a millionth part of a millimetre of plant growth and showed plants have a circulatory system; his instruments showed that even metals react to stimuli and get tired; he invented the wireless coherer before Marconi; he was knighted in 1917 and became FRS in 1920.

questions.q: How did Dr A.P.J. Abdul Kalam cover a long journey from beginning to the post of President of India?
questions.answer: Born at Rameshwaram in 1931, he studied at Schwartz High School and the Madras Institute of Technology (aeronautical engineering). At ISRO (1963–82) he developed the SLV-3 that put Rohini in orbit. As Director of DRDO he led the Integrated Guided Missile Development Programme (Prithvi, Trishul, Akash, Nag, Agni) and made India self-reliant. He received the Bharat Ratna in 1997 and became the eleventh President of India.

or.q: Examine the role of Dr Kalam in making India strong in defence and space sectors.
or.answer: He developed SLV-3 at ISRO and launched Rohini; at DRDO he developed Prithvi, Trishul, Akash, Nag and Agni, making India self-dependent; his light carbon material also helped polio patients and heart patients.

questions.q: Describe the contributions of Srinivasa Ramanujan in the field of mathematics.
questions.answer: Ramanujan, born at Erode in 1887, showed unusual love of numbers; at 13 he read Carr's Synopsis. He wrote results in notebooks and solved problems in the Journal of the Indian Mathematical Society; in 1911 he published a paper on Bernoulli numbers. A clerk at the Madras Port Trust, he wrote to G.H. Hardy giving 120 theorems; Hardy took him to Trinity College, Cambridge, where he formed a team with Hardy and Littlewood, published many papers, became FRS and the first Indian Fellow of Trinity College. He died in 1920.

questions.q: Describe the life and achievements of C.V. Raman.
questions.answer: Raman (born 1888, Tiruchirapalli) topped the IAAS exam and became Assistant Accountant General at 19 but left for physics at Calcutta University. He studied musical instruments (veena, violin, tabla, mridangam) and became FRS (1924). Curious about the sea's blue colour, he found it was scattering of sunlight by water molecules and discovered the Raman Effect, proving light is made of photons, winning the 1930 Nobel Prize, the first Asian to do so. He used his mind as his laboratory and inspired students.

questions.q: Discuss the contributions of Homi Bhabha and Vikram Sarabhai to Indian science.
questions.answer: Bhabha, after cosmic ray research at Cambridge, founded TIFR (1945), BARC and the Apsara reactor, was first chairman of the Atomic Energy Commission and the father of Indian nuclear science. Sarabhai studied cosmic rays under Raman, led the Aryabhata satellite effort, chaired INCOSPAR and AEC, set up TERLS, founded industries and the IIMs and saved crores by making antibiotics and military hardware in India.
